gamerule.propwash.allow_3d_mode.descript: Pilots may use 3D mode (reversible motors, throttle center = zero thrust) once they have unlocked it for themselves. Off: Propwash doesn't let anyone switch it on, for example on race servers where nobody should brake with reverse thrust. Like the flight model, the rule is applied by each pilot's game.
gamerule.propwash.autonomous_rescue.desc: If the return to home (GPS rescue) is running when the pilot leaves – remote put away, flight stopped or game left – the drone keeps flying on its own and lands at the home point. The server only keeps the chunks around the drone loaded and never flies into unexplored terrain. Off: without a pilot the motors stop, as before.
gamerule.propwash.battery_sag.descriptio: On: battery voltage falls as the pack drains, so the drone gets weaker towards the end. Off: resting voltage stays at full charge. Load sag from the internal resistance stays either way.
gamerule.propwash.battery_scale.descript: How long a battery lasts, in percent: 200 twice as long, 50 half as long, 0 infinite (the battery does not drain while flying). The mAh drawn in the OSD count along.
gamerule.propwash.break_impact_scale.des: How clearly a drone feels smashing through glass, in percent: speed lost to the shards it drags along, a kick that knocks it off its attitude (stronger when it hits tilted or with one side only) and shards in the front props. 100 is realistic, 0 leaves only the fracture energy. Only applies with "Drones break blocks"; whether a block breaks and when the drone crashes stays the same.
gamerule.propwash.crash_damage.descripti: Crashes wear the parts down: props first, motors, camera and frame much later. Also covers heat wear and burnt ESCs. Off: parts never wear.
gamerule.propwash.crash_damage_scale.des: How much crashes wear the parts, in percent; 100 is normal. Only with crash damage on.
gamerule.propwash.crash_disarm.descripti: After a hard impact the flight controller shuts the motors off.
gamerule.propwash.crash_tolerance.descri: The impact speed from which a hit counts as a crash, in percent; 100 is normal, higher is more forgiving.
gamerule.propwash.drone_hits_entities.de: Flying drones bounce off animals, monsters and players and hurt them by the force of the impact (mass × speed, at most 5 hearts). Players only with PvP. Off: drones fly through living things.
gamerule.propwash.drone_trails.descripti: On: every flying drone draws a thin, fading trail in its own color (LED strip or paint) – so you can see other pilots even in the FPV view. Landed and disarmed drones draw no trail. Every player can turn the trails off for themselves in the Display tab. Does not change the physics.
gamerule.propwash.drones_break_blocks.de: Fast drones smash glass, glass panes and decorated pots (block tag propwash:drone_breakable) when the impact is strong enough (mass × speed²) and fly on slower. A whoop bounces off, a 5″ goes through a pane from about 42 km/h. Counts as the pilot breaking the block: spawn protection, adventure mode and protection mods apply, glass drops nothing. Off: blocks always stay intact.
gamerule.propwash.drones_generate_chunks: On: when a drone flies past the edge of the world generated so far, new terrain is created there – as if a player walked there (as before). Off: drones only load terrain that already exists. At the edge the drone brakes gently and stops just short of it, the OSD shows “WORLD EDGE” and the FPV view has no holes. Saves server time; GPS rescue without pilot never flies into unexplored terrain anyway. The server config (server.json) can additionally limit generation to permission levels.
gamerule.propwash.freeform_gate_max_size: How large the opening of a freeform gate may be, in blocks per direction: 20 = at most 20 × 20 blocks. Applies when placing and rescanning; placed gates stay as they are. Larger values allow wide halls and caves, smaller ones keep courses tight.
gamerule.propwash.gravity_scale.descript: Gravity for drones in percent of Earth's gravity (100 = 9.81 m/s², 0 = weightless). Higher: drones fall faster and need more throttle to hover; they only take off while their thrust-to-weight ratio from the workbench is above the factor. The workbench and overview always calculate with real Earth gravity.
gamerule.propwash.ground_effect.descript: Extra lift close to the ground.
gamerule.propwash.hardware_limits.descri: On: hot motors throttle back and wear out, and an ESC burns out on arming when the battery has more cells than it allows. Off: no thermal throttling, no heat wear, no burnt ESC.
Drones with analog video: picture and radio link never drop – neither with distance nor behind obstacles. The server's distance limit still applies.
gamerule.propwash.infinite_range_digital: Drones with digital video: picture and radio link never drop – neither with distance nor behind obstacles. The server's distance limit still applies.
gamerule.propwash.invulnerable_pilots.de: On: whoever is flying a drone takes no damage – for events where pilots should stand protected at the side. Off (default): the pilot's body stays a normal player; gravity, mobs, other players, falls, lava, drowning and hunger work as usual. The void and /kill always apply.
gamerule.propwash.max_video_channels.des: How many video transmitters may be on air at the same time – like the frequency board at a race. When every channel is taken, no further drone can take off until a pilot lands. Pilots already in the air keep flying. 0 = unlimited.
gamerule.propwash.part_compatibility.des: On: the workbench, imports and field service only build drones from parts that would fit together in reality (mounts, prop size, battery for the frame, accessory mounts). Off: every part fits every other. The notes stay visible, the drone flies with the real data of its parts and doesn't count for leaderboards. Overvoltage is still governed by “Hardware limits”.
gamerule.propwash.prop_strikes.descripti: A prop clipping an obstacle slows its motor and sends the drone tumbling.
gamerule.propwash.prop_wash.description: Turbulence when a drone descends through its own downwash.
gamerule.propwash.save_assisted_laps.des: On: laps and races flown with a flight aid – altitude or position hold, GPS rescue, changed world rules, creative drone, parts that only fit with “Parts must fit” off, or a goggles latency below the video transmitter's – are saved anyway: the leaderboard, personal best, ghost and race display show them with the badge “Assisted” and the reason. In the leaderboard they get their own section below the unassisted times and never become a record. Off: assisted laps don't count (as before).
gamerule.propwash.signal_repeaters.descr: How many signal repeaters may pass video and control on between pilot and drone in a row (at most 4). Each repeater reaches 128 blocks, and the signal goes through walls and ceilings just as it otherwise would; laps flown over repeaters count for leaderboards. 0 = repeaters off.
gamerule.propwash.turbulence.description: Rough air: gusts and the shaking in the drone's own downwash. Off: the wind blows steadily.
gamerule.propwash.wind.description: Strength of wind and gusts. Off: calm. Mild: wind depends on weather and height, almost calm under a roof (default). Windy: twice as strong. Storm: three times as strong – in a thunderstorm small drones can barely fly against it.

propwash.creative.param.prop.blades.tip: Number of blades for sound and losses of small props. Thrust and torque come from the two coefficients below.

propwash.creative.param.prop.mass_g.tip: Weight of one prop. Heavy props spin up more slowly (motor response).

propwash.drone.service.hint_swap_one: Click a slot to swap that prop

propwash.drone.service.hint_too_small: Too small for this frame (min %s mm)
propwash.drone.service.props_help_1: Click with a prop: swap that slot
propwash.drone.service.props_help_3: Old props go back to your inventory
propwash.drone.service.receiver.cleared: Receiver: reset. Click the drone with your remote to bind it again.
propwash.drone.service.receiver.confirm: Click again: really reset the binding. Every remote has to bind again afterwards.
propwash.drone.service.receiver.other: Receiver: bound to another pilot. Click the drone with your remote to fly it.
propwash.drone.service.receiver.pilot: Receiver: bound to you. Your remote connects right away – even after the workbench and picking up.
propwash.drone.service.receiver.unbound: Receiver: no stored binding yet. Click the drone once with your remote and the binding is kept.
propwash.drone.session.no_radio: No radio connected – the drone stays in failsafe
propwash.drone.session.no_video: No picture: your goggles receive %1$s, %2$s sends %3$s. Take them off to fly line of sight.
propwash.drone.session.refused_video: Not connected: your goggles receive %1$s, %2$s sends %3$s. Wear matching goggles or take them off for line of sight.
propwash.drone.session.switched_los: Goggles off – continuing line of sight
propwash.drone.tooltip.weights: Dry weight %s g · all-up weight %s g (with battery)
propwash.drone_render.fpv_ducts.tip: Shows the ducts of your whoop or cinewhoop in the camera image exactly where they would be visible for this camera position, uptilt and field of view – the front ducts in the lower corners, because the camera sits above them like on real ones. Display only, no effect on the flight model.
propwash.drone_render.fpv_props.tip: Shows your own props in the camera image exactly where they would be visible for this camera position, uptilt and field of view: the tips at the edge on a 5 inch with steep uptilt, nothing on a deadcat. Display only, no effect on the flight model.
propwash.drone_render.shadow.tip: Drone shadows on the ground. With a shader pack the pack draws the shadows, and in FPV flight your own drone casts one too. Off: no drone shadows, not even with a shader pack.
propwash.drone_render.size_notice.messag: Drones now show at their real size (1.0× instead of 1.75×), so their speed looks real. To change it back: Configurator → Display → Drone size.
propwash.drone_render.size_notice.title: Drones now at real size
propwash.dust.enabled.tip: Subtle dust under the rotors when a drone flies close to the ground, a faint spray over water. Follows Minecraft's Particles setting and is off at Minimal.
propwash.dust.intensity.tip: How much dust the rotors stir up. The cap on simultaneous particles always stays active.
propwash.guide.index.tip: Tip: hold %s over a Propwash item in any inventory to open its Flight school scene

propwash.guide.scene.action_cam.descript: Real MP4 videos with motor sound from your FPV flights
propwash.guide.scene.action_cam.step.fla: No video: the Action Cam (Flashback) records your FPV camera's path for the replay mod Flashback (Fabric only). Same button as above.
propwash.guide.scene.action_cam.step.lib: After stopping, the MP4 is saved in the background. In the configurator, “Browse recordings” lists every video with a thumbnail.
propwash.guide.scene.action_cam.step.mou: In the workbench the action cam goes into the “Accessory top” slot. The Light runs on the flight battery, the Heavy has its own and stabilizes.
propwash.guide.scene.action_cam.step.rec: While flying FPV the “Record” key starts and stops the video. At the top right of the OSD, ● REC counts the recording time.
propwash.guide.scene.action_cam.step.swi: In the “Modes” tab you put “Record” on the radio: a switch records while it is on, a button starts and stops with every press.
propwash.guide.scene.action_cam.title: Action cam: recording videos
propwash.guide.scene.bandos.description: Find abandoned buildings to fly freestyle in
propwash.guide.scene.bandos.step.chest.t: Some bandos hide a chest with Propwash parts, often used – sometimes up on a catwalk or in a hayloft.
propwash.guide.scene.bandos.step.find.te: Bandos are abandoned buildings: barns, factories, water towers, piers or oil rigs. They are rare, match their biome and are never the same.
propwash.guide.scene.bandos.step.fly.tex: Doors, windows, holes in the roof, catwalks and gaps between beams are made for flying through – perfect for gaps and power loops.
With cheats, /locate structure #propwash:bandos shows the nearest bando. They only exist when the world generates structures.
propwash.guide.scene.bandos.title: Bandos: abandoned spots
propwash.guide.scene.battery.callout.cha: The drone takes the pack and its charge
propwash.guide.scene.battery.callout.che: Charges every pack: LiPo, LiHV and Li-Ion
propwash.guide.scene.battery.callout.fra: The frame carries at most 230 g of battery, this one weighs 420 g – the drone refuses it
propwash.guide.scene.battery.callout.non: Without a battery the drone can't be connected
propwash.guide.scene.battery.callout.rul: World rule “Parts must fit” off: then this pack fits too
propwash.guide.scene.battery.description: Swap packs, check the fit and charge them
propwash.guide.scene.battery.step.charge: The charger charges every pack, Li-Ion too: up to four at once, about 1–3 minutes by size. Click it with a pack in hand to insert it.
propwash.guide.scene.battery.step.fit.te: The frame decides which packs fit: cell count and maximum weight. The drone refuses a pack that is too heavy. The tooltip (Shift) shows what fits.
propwash.guide.scene.battery.step.land.t: When the pack runs low, land and disconnect. While the drone is armed or being flown, the battery stays locked.
propwash.guide.scene.battery.step.menu.t: Sneak + right-click the drone to open its service menu: take the battery out or put a fitting one in; the four props sit next to it.
propwash.guide.scene.battery.step.swap.t: Faster with a fitting pack in hand: sneak + right-click inserts it directly and the old one goes to your inventory.
propwash.guide.scene.battery.title: Swapping and charging batteries
propwash.guide.scene.bind.callout.fpv: Remote bound, matching goggles on: FPV
propwash.guide.scene.bind.callout.keep: Workbench, pick up, place: the binding stays
propwash.guide.scene.bind.callout.los: Goggles off: line of sight always works
propwash.guide.scene.bind.callout.mismat: Analog goggles, digital drone: the remote refuses
propwash.guide.scene.bind.callout.remote: Remote in hand: click the drone
propwash.guide.scene.bind.callout.system: Digital goggles, digital drone: a match
propwash.guide.scene.bind.callout.takeov: If another pilot clicks it with their remote, it binds to them
propwash.guide.scene.bind.description: Bind the remote – the goggles only have to match
propwash.guide.scene.bind.step.keep.text: The receiver remembers you: workbench, pick-up, placing and restarts change nothing. A new flight controller needs a bind.
propwash.guide.scene.bind.step.match.tex: When binding and starting, the remote checks your goggles: they must receive the drone's video. Wrong goggles: refused. No goggles: line of sight.
propwash.guide.scene.bind.step.remote.te: Hold the remote and right-click the placed drone. The remote remembers the drone, its receiver remembers you.
propwash.guide.scene.bind.step.start.tex: Right-click into the air with the bound remote. With matching goggles on you fly FPV, without goggles line of sight.
propwash.guide.scene.bind.step.wear.text: Goggles are not bound: just put them on – right-click into the air or use the head slot. The remote sees which goggles you wear.
propwash.guide.scene.bind.title: Binding the remote, wearing goggles
propwash.guide.scene.configurator.callou: Angle: let go – it levels out
Configurator only when landed and disarmed
Wind world rule: off to storm
Applies to everyone in this world
propwash.guide.scene.configurator.descri: Understand sticks, rates, PID and flight modes
propwash.guide.scene.configurator.step.c: Under “Commands” in the “Modes” tab you put your own commands on switches or keys, like /time set night. They run as if typed, with your rights.
propwash.guide.scene.configurator.step.m: Angle levels the drone when you let go, Acro holds any angle for flips and rolls. Horizon mixes both.
propwash.guide.scene.configurator.step.p: The PID controller keeps the drone on the course your sticks command. Its values are derived automatically from the build.
propwash.guide.scene.configurator.step.r: Rates set how fast the drone turns: same stick input, faster rotation. Expo makes the center finer. Presets are in the “Rates” tab.
propwash.guide.scene.configurator.step.s: Right stick: pitch and roll, left stick: throttle and yaw (mode 2). Each stick movement turns the drone around one axis.
In the “Modes” tab you put arming, flight mode, LEDs and more on radio switches. Every function also has a key – the last input counts.
propwash.guide.scene.configurator.step.w: Gravity, wind, battery and crash damage apply to the whole world: World rules tab with presets. The host and whoever may use /gamerule change them.
propwash.guide.scene.configurator.title: Configurator: rates, PID, modes
propwash.guide.scene.course_elements.cal: Around behind the flag and back
In from the top, out through the glowing side
Climb, dive in, out the side
Side, height and scoring width with the mouse wheel
Right around: the flag stays on your right
Arrows on the ground: pass here – the red cross is the wrong side
propwash.guide.scene.course_elements.des: Poles, turn flags and cubes for your course
propwash.guide.scene.course_elements.ste: Fly the cube like in MultiGP races: dive in from the top and out through the glowing side. You choose which side is the exit.
Sneak + right-click with the element or the course tool: the mouse wheel sets heading, side or exit, height and scoring width, Enter applies.
Fly around the flag: past it, around behind it and back on the other side. The arrows on the ground show left or right around.
The next element glows green like a gate. The HUD shows a wrong side or direction in red, and the element only counts once you fly it right.
Set up the poles and append them in order with the course tool. When a pole follows a pole, the tool switches the side – your slalom.
propwash.guide.scene.creative_drone.desc: Set every value of the flight model freely
propwash.guide.scene.creative_drone.step: The creative inventory holds the Creative Flight Controller. It fits every frame and turns the other parts into a creative drone.
Hold the drone or fly it, then open the configurator: in the “Drone Editor” tab masses, geometry, props, motors and battery are free.
Same physics, free values: saved values apply at once, in flight after disarming. Creative drones do not count for leaderboards.
Start from any preset or your own base parts, keep templates and share them as a code. Set rates and PIDs as usual.
propwash.guide.scene.drone_build.callout: Drone workbench: top-down slots, 3D preview and flight stats
Bind the remote: right-click the drone with the remote in hand
Empty batteries charge in the charger
Ready to fly! The drone waits in the result slot.
Red: error – the Li-Ion pack is too heavy for this frame
Landed? Stop with the “Stop FPV flight” key or another right-click
Frame – the backbone. It decides which parts fit.
Four identical motors on the arms
Four identical propellers on the motors
World rule “Parts must fit” off: then this pack fits too
Stack: flight controller with ESCs, stores the tune
Stats: weight without and with battery, thrust/weight, flight time, top speed
Video unit: camera and transmitter, analog or digital
Yellow: warning – 4S fits, but the drone gets weak
propwash.guide.scene.drone_build.descrip: From parts to a ready-to-fly drone
propwash.guide.scene.drone_build.step.be: Place a drone workbench and open it with a right-click. This is where you build a drone from parts – and take it apart again if needed.
propwash.guide.scene.drone_build.step.do: Once every slot holds a matching part, the finished drone appears in the result slot. It keeps the installed battery and its charge.
propwash.guide.scene.drone_build.step.fl: Right-click into the air with the bound remote to fly: FPV with matching goggles on, line of sight without goggles. Land first, then stop.
propwash.guide.scene.drone_build.step.fr: The frame goes into the center slot, the stack (flight controller with ESCs) into the slot above it.
propwash.guide.scene.drone_build.step.mo: Fill all four motor slots and all four propeller slots on the arms – each set must be four identical parts.
propwash.guide.scene.drone_build.step.pl: Right-click a block with the drone in your hand to place it. Then bind the remote by right-clicking the drone with it.
Place it and bind the remote
propwash.guide.scene.drone_build.step.st: The workbench shows weight without and with battery, thrust/weight, flight time and top speed. Red: doesn't fit. Yellow: flies, but has weaknesses.
propwash.guide.scene.drone_build.step.vi: The video unit at the nose decides the video system. The battery must fit the frame; it only charges in the battery charger.
propwash.guide.scene.drone_build.title: Building a drone at the workbench
propwash.guide.scene.fpv_los.callout.fol: Your view follows the drone by itself
propwash.guide.scene.fpv_los.callout.hud: Remote HUD: battery, signal, flight mode
propwash.guide.scene.fpv_los.callout.loc: Back to FPV: put matching goggles back on
propwash.guide.scene.fpv_los.callout.osd: In view: OSD with battery, signal, flight mode and time
propwash.guide.scene.fpv_los.callout.swi: Goggles off: continuing line of sight
propwash.guide.scene.fpv_los.description: Through the drone's camera or with your own eyes
propwash.guide.scene.fpv_los.step.fpv.te: With matching goggles on you see the drone's camera feed. Your body stays put with the remote in hand – and can still get hurt.
propwash.guide.scene.fpv_los.step.hud.te: Instead of the goggles OSD, a compact radio HUD shows battery, signal and flight mode. Walking and looking around are locked in flight.
propwash.guide.scene.fpv_los.step.los.te: Without goggles you fly line of sight with your own eyes. Your view turns smoothly and automatically towards the drone.
propwash.guide.scene.fpv_los.step.stop.t: Land, then press the “Stop FPV flight” key or right-click with the remote again. The drone stays bound.
propwash.guide.scene.fpv_los.title: FPV and line-of-sight flight
propwash.guide.scene.gate_free.callout.f: The blocks around it are the frame – the edge glows
Counts only inside the opening · at most 20 × 20 blocks (world rule)
propwash.guide.scene.gate_free.descripti: Diagonal, tilted, as a diamond, any size and freeform gates
propwash.guide.scene.gate_free.step.angl: Yaw turns the gate like a compass, pitch tilts it, roll turns the opening within itself. The gate stays on its surface.
propwash.guide.scene.gate_free.step.edit: Sneak + right-click a gate holding a gate or the course tool: keep walking, the mouse wheel adjusts live, Enter applies, Alt frees the mouse.
propwash.guide.scene.gate_free.step.free: No frame: right-click the edge of an opening and the blocks around it bound the gate. Caves, hallways and windows become course gates.
propwash.guide.scene.gate_free.step.size: Width and height of the opening go from 1 to 16 blocks in half steps. The item only sets the starting size.
propwash.guide.scene.gate_free.step.step: “Rotate gate” turns standing and hanging gates by the step set in the Racing tab: 90, 45, 15 or 5 degrees.
propwash.guide.scene.gate_free.title: Rotating gates freely
propwash.guide.scene.gripper.callout.cap: Up to 400 g in 4 stacks – never more than half the spare thrust
propwash.guide.scene.gripper.callout.cra: Hard crash: the cargo falls out
propwash.guide.scene.gripper.callout.hea: Cargo adds weight: more throttle, shorter flights
propwash.guide.scene.gripper.callout.lan: Disarmed on the ground: cargo set down
propwash.guide.scene.gripper.callout.low: Hover low: below one block it grabs
propwash.guide.scene.gripper.callout.swi: Or the “Drop cargo” switch in the Modes tab
propwash.guide.scene.gripper.description: Pick up items in flight, carry and drop them
propwash.guide.scene.gripper.step.auto.t: Landing and disarming sets everything down. In a hard crash the cargo falls out, nothing is lost.
propwash.guide.scene.gripper.step.drop.t: Open it over the target: the “Cargo drop” key or a switch on the radio. The items fall with the drone's momentum, e.g. into a hopper.
In the workbench the gripper goes into the “Bottom accessory” slot, in place of the LED strip. It weighs 18 g and hangs under the nose.
propwash.guide.scene.gripper.step.pickup: Arm and hover low over the items. Whatever lies under the drone goes into the gripper – as long as weight and stacks allow.
propwash.guide.scene.gripper.title: Gripper: collecting items
propwash.guide.scene.hold.callout.baro: The barometer measures air pressure – that gives the altitude
propwash.guide.scene.hold.callout.bobbin: Never quite still: it bobs about ±0.3–1 m
propwash.guide.scene.hold.callout.climb: Throttle up: climbs slowly at the climb rate
propwash.guide.scene.hold.callout.gps: GPS: accurate to 1–3 m, ten times per second
propwash.guide.scene.hold.callout.never_: Never perfect: altitude ±1 m, position a few meters
propwash.guide.scene.hold.callout.no_gps: OSD "NO GPS": only ALTHOLD left, it drifts
propwash.guide.scene.hold.callout.roof: A roof above the drone hides the satellites
propwash.guide.scene.hold.callout.tuning: PID Tuning: values for ALTHOLD and POSHOLD
propwash.guide.scene.hold.callout.wind: Wind pushes it away, it creeps back slowly
propwash.guide.scene.hold.description: ALTHOLD and POSHOLD: what they can do and where they fail
propwash.guide.scene.hold.step.althold.t: A switch or the key turns on ALTHOLD: the drone levels itself and holds its altitude with the barometer.
propwash.guide.scene.hold.step.climb.tex: Throttle near the hold position keeps the altitude. More throttle climbs, less descends – both at a limited rate so it stays calm.
propwash.guide.scene.hold.step.limits.te: Both modes help but are no autopilot: gusts, flying near the ground and speed disturb the sensors. Tune them in PID Tuning.
propwash.guide.scene.hold.step.no_gps.te: Under blocks, in caves, indoors or in deep ravines the receiver sees few satellites. Then POSHOLD does not work.
propwash.guide.scene.hold.step.poshold.t: With a GPS fix POSHOLD also holds the spot. Roll and pitch move the drone, releasing the sticks holds the new position.
propwash.guide.scene.hold.title: Altitude and position hold
propwash.guide.scene.mode_3d.callout.arm: Arm only with the throttle centered
propwash.guide.scene.mode_3d.callout.bin: Then bind it to a radio switch or a key
propwash.guide.scene.mode_3d.callout.cen: Center (1500 µs): no thrust, props at idle
propwash.guide.scene.mode_3d.callout.con: Upside down, pitch and yaw feel reversed from your view
propwash.guide.scene.mode_3d.callout.dow: Throttle down: motors spin backwards, thrust pushes down
propwash.guide.scene.mode_3d.callout.fli: Roll until inverted, throttle to the center meanwhile
propwash.guide.scene.mode_3d.callout.hov: Hover: throttle a little above center
Inverted hover: throttle a little below center
propwash.guide.scene.mode_3d.callout.lif: Throttle down: reverse thrust lifts it off inverted
propwash.guide.scene.mode_3d.callout.off: 3D off: throttle center now means half throttle, it climbs
propwash.guide.scene.mode_3d.callout.pun: Throttle all the way down: down faster than free fall
propwash.guide.scene.mode_3d.callout.res: Like angle mode to get out of trouble: flip the switch
propwash.guide.scene.mode_3d.callout.rul: Servers can forbid 3D with a world rule
propwash.guide.scene.mode_3d.callout.sav: Saves split-S and power loops that are too low
propwash.guide.scene.mode_3d.callout.up: Throttle up: forward thrust, the drone climbs
propwash.guide.scene.mode_3d.callout.ups: Landed upside down? With 3D you don't need to flip it
propwash.guide.scene.mode_3d.callout.wea: Normal props manage only about half the thrust in reverse
propwash.guide.scene.mode_3d.description: Reverse thrust: fly inverted, save loops, take off inverted
propwash.guide.scene.mode_3d.step.invert: Upside down, throttle a little below center holds the height. 3D works with acro and horizon; angle always levels the drone upright.
Full reverse thrust pushes down, faster than free fall. Save a move that came out too low or punch down before a bar.
Reverse thrust to save a move
propwash.guide.scene.mode_3d.step.switch: Switch or key off: normal throttle applies at once. Altitude hold, GPS rescue and failsafe always fly without 3D.
propwash.guide.scene.mode_3d.step.takeof: If the drone lies upside down, arm with the throttle centered and give reverse throttle: it takes off inverted, then roll it over.
propwash.guide.scene.mode_3d.step.thrott: In 3D mode the throttle center means no thrust. Above it the props push up, below it the motors spin backwards and push down.
propwash.guide.scene.mode_3d.step.unlock: 3D is a flight mode of its own. Unlock it once in the configurator, then bind it to a switch or a key like angle mode.
propwash.guide.scene.mode_3d.title: 3D mode
propwash.guide.scene.race.callout.dive: Dive gate: lies flat on the wall, fly through from above
propwash.guide.scene.race.callout.diving: Dive: the dive gate only counts downwards
propwash.guide.scene.race.callout.double: Double gate: top and bottom are separate course gates
propwash.guide.scene.race.callout.hangin: Hangs from two straps under the ceiling
propwash.guide.scene.race.callout.ladder: Ladder: zig-zag upwards – stack it while looking back to flip the gate
propwash.guide.scene.race.callout.lap: Lap done: lap time, best lap, split
propwash.guide.scene.race.callout.next: After each gate, green moves on
propwash.guide.scene.race.callout.side: Side gate: one post on the wall, fly along the wall
propwash.guide.scene.race.description: Place gates, set a course, fly laps
propwash.guide.scene.race.step.course.te: Click the gates in order with the course tool; the first one is start and finish. To take one out, use “Adjust gate”.
propwash.guide.scene.race.step.fly.text: The next gate of your race glows green, all others white. Fly through them in the right direction and order.
propwash.guide.scene.race.step.fly.title: Through the gates
propwash.guide.scene.race.step.lap.text: Back through gate 1 after all gates: lap complete! Races have three laps by default. Leaderboard: /propwash race leaderboard
propwash.guide.scene.race.step.lap.title: Lap and lap time
propwash.guide.scene.race.step.mount.tex: Gates also go on walls and ceilings. Holding a gate, the Rotate gate key turns it; while sneaking it switches the mount, e.g. to a dive gate.
propwash.guide.scene.race.step.place.tex: Hold a gate item and right-click the ground. The opening faces your view direction – that is the direction to fly through.
propwash.guide.scene.race.step.stack.tex: Right-click a gate with a gate to put it on top – like a ladder with a shared middle bar. Each one stays its own course gate.
propwash.guide.scene.race.step.start.tex: Gate 1 pulses green while you are not racing. A start countdown can be switched on in the “Race” tab.
propwash.guide.scene.race.title: Gates, courses and racing
propwash.guide.scene.recovery.callout.ai: Arm angle 180°: armed again in the air
Disarmed: it falls and tips over
propwash.guide.scene.recovery.callout.fu: Full strength up to about 800 blocks
propwash.guide.scene.recovery.callout.vi: Behind the pillar: picture gets noisy or freezes
propwash.guide.scene.recovery.callout.wa: Solid blocks weaken the picture a lot
propwash.guide.scene.recovery.descriptio: Flip back, fly on and find your drone again
propwash.guide.scene.recovery.step.air.t: Disarmed mid-flight? With the max arm angle at 180° (configurator, “Configuration” tab) you can arm in any attitude – even in the air.
propwash.guide.scene.recovery.step.beepe: Lost in tall grass? While connected and disarmed, the drone beeps with the locator beeper – just follow the sound.
propwash.guide.scene.recovery.step.crash: After a hard impact the flight controller shuts the motors off. Often the drone ends up on its back.
Once disarmed and still, “Flip drone upright” sets it back on its feet. Arming needs the throttle fully down and at most 25° of tilt.
propwash.guide.scene.recovery.step.range: Full strength up to about 800 blocks, gone around 1200 (schematic). Creative, creative goggles or the Infinite range world rule: no limit.
propwash.guide.scene.recovery.step.walls: Depending on the video unit, the picture reaches about 250–520 blocks. Leaves weaken it a little, a trunk more, walls, hills and water a lot.
propwash.guide.scene.recovery.title: Crashes, range and signal
propwash.guide.scene.repair.callout.bend: PC: bends, flies on but worse
propwash.guide.scene.repair.callout.crac: Hard PC, glass nylon: breaks into pieces
propwash.guide.scene.repair.callout.crea: Off only with the Crash damage world rule
propwash.guide.scene.repair.callout.menu: Service menu: props laid out like the drone
propwash.guide.scene.repair.callout.pair: Two damaged props of the same kind
propwash.guide.scene.repair.callout.recy: Broken parts into the salvage slot: recycle
propwash.guide.scene.repair.callout.sum: Conditions add up plus 5 %, at most 100 %
propwash.guide.scene.repair.callout.swap: New props on, ready to fly
propwash.guide.scene.repair.description: Crashes wear parts down – swap and repair props
propwash.guide.scene.repair.step.bench.t: Motors, camera, frame, flight controller and battery are swapped at the workbench: take the drone apart, check the condition, replace the part.
propwash.guide.scene.repair.step.combine: Don't throw old props away: craft two damaged ones of the same kind together or put them in a grindstone – conditions add up, plus 5 %.
propwash.guide.scene.repair.step.crash.t: A prop shrugs off light bumps. Hard crashes damage every part: props first, motors much later, frame and electronics last.
A broken prop gives almost no thrust – the drone can't fly like this. Bent or cracked props cost thrust and add vibration to the picture.
propwash.guide.scene.repair.step.fly.tex: With fresh props the drone flies like new. Crash damage can only be switched off for the whole world: the Crash damage world rule.
propwash.guide.scene.repair.step.materia: PC bends and flies on, but worse; hard PC and glass-fiber nylon break into pieces; bi-blend sits in between. Carbon rarely breaks – then fully.
propwash.guide.scene.repair.step.swap.te: Sneak + right-click opens the service menu, even with props in hand. Drop a prop on a slot to swap it; the old ones go to your inventory.
propwash.guide.scene.repair.step.swap.ti: Swap props in the service menu

Five rings at different heights: climb, sink, climb.
Throttle sets the height, tilt sets the speed. Start climbing early.
propwash.guide.training.lesson.arm.descr: Arm, let the props spin for 2 s and disarm again.
propwash.guide.training.lesson.arm.tip: You can only arm with the throttle all the way down. Disarm only while the drone sits on the ground.
propwash.guide.training.lesson.arm.tip_m: Throttle keys or mouse wheel all the way down, then arm. The mouse only steers while you fly and no menu is open.
propwash.guide.training.lesson.arm.title: Arming
propwash.guide.training.lesson.combo.des: Three tricks back to back without a break.
propwash.guide.training.lesson.combo.tip: At most 3 s between tricks – flip, roll, flip is quickest.
propwash.guide.training.lesson.dive_gate: Climb over the flat gate and dive straight down through it.
Above the gate, nose down, almost no throttle, dive through and pull out early.
propwash.guide.training.lesson.figure_ei: A figure eight around two pillars through seven rings.
Keep your height steady and look for the next ring before you pass the current one.
propwash.guide.training.lesson.final_exa: Two rings, a trick, a dive gate and a landing on the pad.
Everything from the chapters combined. Take enough height in the trick area.
propwash.guide.training.lesson.flip.desc: Do a flip on the pitch axis inside the trick area.
propwash.guide.training.lesson.flip.tip: Above 5 m: cut the throttle, full pitch, then throttle up to catch it. Best in Acro mode.
propwash.guide.training.lesson.flip.tip_: In Acro: cut the throttle and pull the mouse back briskly until the drone has gone around once, then stop the mouse and throttle up. The faster the mouse, the faster the flip.
propwash.guide.training.lesson.gate_line: Six gates in a line as fast as you can – with split times.
Splits compare with your best run: green is faster, red is slower.
propwash.guide.training.lesson.hover.des: Climb into the box above the start pad and stay inside for 6 s.
propwash.guide.training.lesson.hover.tip: Raise the throttle slowly until the drone lifts off, then make small corrections. In Angle mode it levels itself.
Fine-tune the throttle with the mouse wheel. In Angle mode the mouse tilts the drone and it slowly levels out again – the middle mouse button levels it at once.
propwash.guide.training.lesson.land.desc: Fly to the pad ahead, touch down gently and disarm.
propwash.guide.training.lesson.land.tip: Slow down before the pad (pitch back), then sink with a little less throttle. Stars depend on how close you land to the center.
propwash.guide.training.lesson.low_fligh: Five flat rings just above the ground.
Little tilt and a soft throttle hand – ground effect lifts you slightly.
propwash.guide.training.lesson.power_loo: A full backwards loop under power.
Come in with speed, add throttle and pull back until you are upside down at the top, then keep pulling and catch it.
Throttle up and pull the mouse back evenly until the loop is round. A large mouse pad helps.
propwash.guide.training.lesson.precision: Six small rings in an S curve – every touch ends the attempt.
Slow is fast here: better clean than clipping a frame.
propwash.guide.training.lesson.roll.desc: Do a roll on the roll axis inside the trick area.
propwash.guide.training.lesson.roll.tip: Like the flip, but with the roll stick. Level out straight after.
propwash.guide.training.lesson.roll.tip_: In Acro: swipe the mouse sideways briskly until the drone has turned once. When the mouse stops, the rotation stops.
propwash.guide.training.lesson.short_cou: Two laps of a loop with six gates.
Gate 1 starts the lap clock. The second lap compares every split with the first.
propwash.guide.training.lesson.slalom.de: Six offset gates in a zigzag.
propwash.guide.training.lesson.slalom.ti: Smooth lines beat sharp hooks: turn in early and take the gates at an angle.
propwash.guide.training.lesson.split_s.d: Half roll upside down, then pull through downwards and fly back.
propwash.guide.training.lesson.split_s.t: Bring enough height: a split-S costs a few meters.
Fly forward through five rings in a row.
Pitching forward tilts the drone – add a little throttle or it sinks.
Push the mouse forward a little and leave it there, the drone flies straight. Pull it back a bit to brake.
propwash.guide.training.lesson.turns.des: A wide right-hand turn through six rings.
propwash.guide.training.lesson.turns.tip: Clean turns combine roll and yaw: a little right roll, then follow with yaw.
Move the mouse slightly sideways and tap the side key to yaw at the same time – small mouse movements are enough.
propwash.guide.training.lesson.yaw.descr: Turn inside the box to face the four glowing pillars in turn.
propwash.guide.training.lesson.yaw.tip: Yaw only turns the nose. Hold your height with the throttle and stay inside the box.
propwash.guide.training.lesson.yaw.tip_m: Yaw is on the side keys. Tap rather than hold – or pick “Mouse left/right: Yaw” in the Receiver tab.

propwash.input.layout.tooltip: Gamepad layout uses SDL's standard mapping (sticks, triggers, buttons). Raw axes reads the axes directly, which is right for radios in USB joystick mode. Switching resets the mapping to defaults.
propwash.input.leds.held_off: LEDs stay off: the “%s” switch on your radio is active
propwash.input.leds.no_strip: This drone has no LED strip
propwash.input.modes.acro_device: On while Angle and Horizon are off
propwash.input.modes.assign.tooltip: Shortcut: click, then flip the switch into the position in which the function should be active. Source and range are filled in automatically.
propwash.input.modes.commands.hint: Flipping the switch runs its command as if typed in chat – only while flying, never with a menu open.
propwash.input.modes.desc.acro: The drone keeps its angle until you steer back – nothing levels it out. Full control for freestyle and racing. On while Angle and Horizon are off; key or switch, the last input counts.
propwash.input.modes.desc.alt_hold: Self-levels like Angle and holds altitude with the barometer, never exactly (about ±0.3–1 m). Throttle near its position when switched on holds, more climbs, less descends – at a limited rate. Values in the "PID Tuning" tab.
propwash.input.modes.desc.angle: Release the sticks and the drone levels out by itself; the tilt is limited. The easiest mode to learn.
propwash.input.modes.desc.arm: Switches the motors on and off. Arm with the throttle at zero; disarming stops the props at once.
propwash.input.modes.desc.beeper: Switches the locator beeper on or off – to find a crashed drone by its sound.
propwash.input.modes.desc.blackbox: Logs the flight to the blackbox only while the switch is on, like the BLACKBOX mode in Betaflight. Without an assignment the blackbox logs every armed flight once it is switched on in the “Blackbox” tab.
propwash.input.modes.desc.cargo_drop: Opens the gripper and drops the cargo, best on a button. Needs a gripper on the bottom mount; without an assignment the “Cargo drop” key (Enter) drops it, and landing or a hard crash opens it too.
propwash.input.modes.desc.command: Runs a Minecraft command of your choice when you flip the switch or press the key – exactly as if you typed it in chat, with your own permissions – and optionally a second one when you flip it back. Only while you fly a drone and no menu is open.
propwash.input.modes.desc.flip_over: Turns a crashed drone upright again. It has to be disarmed and lying still.
propwash.input.modes.desc.horizon: Levels out near the stick center like Angle, but full stick deflection still rolls or flips the drone.
propwash.input.modes.desc.leds_off: Switches the LED strip and the FPV headlight off while the function is active – like LED_LOW in Betaflight. Other players see it too. Without an assignment the LEDs glow as set in the “LED strip” tab.
propwash.input.modes.desc.mode_3d: Reversible motors like with 3D ESCs: throttle down = full reverse thrust, center = idle, up = full forward thrust. Fly upside down, save botched loops and take off upside down after a crash. Arm only with the throttle centered; switching it off brings normal throttle back at once.
propwash.input.modes.desc.pos_hold: Holds altitude and position with GPS (1–3 m accurate, drifts and corrects slowly). Needs open sky: under blocks, in caves or ravines there are too few satellites, then the OSD shows "NO GPS" and only altitude is held.
propwash.input.modes.desc.race_restart: Restarts the race: the current run is canceled, and flying through gate 1 starts the new one.
propwash.input.modes.desc.record: Starts and stops the action cam recording while you fly FPV. A switch records while it is on; a button starts and stops with every press. Needs an action cam on top of the frame; find your videos in the “Action cam” tab under “Recordings”.
propwash.input.modes.desc.rescue: GPS rescue: the drone climbs, flies back to the home point and lands. Switch it off again to take over.
propwash.input.modes.desc.set_home: Stores where the drone is now as the home point that GPS rescue flies back to.
propwash.input.modes.effect.cargo_drop: Opens the gripper and drops the cargo
propwash.input.modes.effect.horizon: Self-levels, but full stick still flips
propwash.input.modes.effect.mode_3d: Throttle center = zero thrust, down = reverse thrust
propwash.input.modes.effect.race_restart: Restarts the race – back to gate 1
propwash.input.modes.effect.rescue: Flies back to the home point

propwash.input.modes.hint_keyboard: Every function has its own key – change them in the Keys tab.
propwash.input.modes.invert.tooltip_arm: If this turns Arm on, the drone stays disarmed until the switch has been turned off and on again.
propwash.input.modes.invert.tooltip_axis: Inverted: reverses the switch – positions swap their order, the range is mirrored at 1500 µs.
propwash.input.modes.invert.tooltip_butt: Inverted: swaps on and off – active while the button is released.
propwash.input.modes.invert.tooltip_togg: Inverted: swaps on and off of the latch – every press still toggles.
propwash.input.modes.key_override: %s chosen by key – flipping a mode switch on the radio takes over again
propwash.input.modes.key_override_3d_off: 3D mode off by key – the radio switch counts again as soon as you move it.
propwash.input.modes.key_override_3d_on: 3D mode on by key – the radio switch counts again as soon as you move it.
propwash.input.modes.legend.led: Lamp: lights up while the function is on
propwash.input.modes.mode_3d.unlock.tool: Unlocks 3D mode for you (personal setting). Then bind it to a switch or the key like the other modes. Whether it is allowed in a world is decided by the world rule “3D mode allowed”.
propwash.input.modes.mode_3d.unlock_firs: Unlock it first, then bind it to a switch or the key.
propwash.input.modes.no_device_short: No radio: turn on keyboard flight in the Receiver tab.
propwash.input.modes.on_stick.tooltip: Warning: %s is the %s stick channel. This assignment switches while you steer. Pick an AUX channel or a button.
propwash.input.modes.open_controls.toolt: Opens the Keys tab: change every Propwash key there.
propwash.input.modes.page.commands.toolt: Custom commands 1–8: put your own Minecraft commands on switches and keys
propwash.input.modes.page.flight.tooltip: Flight functions: arming, flight modes, rescue and more
propwash.input.modes.range_tooltip: Active from %s to %s µs · now %s µs
propwash.input.modes.source.tooltip: AUX channel (any axis that is not a stick) or a radio button. Scroll wheel or Shift+click steps backwards.
propwash.input.modes.unbound_hint: Not assigned – pick a source or click “Flip switch”.
propwash.input.mouse.deadzone.label: Mouse deadzone
propwash.input.mouse.deadzone.tooltip: The tiniest mouse movements around center do nothing. Helps you fly calmly in a straight line.
propwash.input.mouse.demo.forward.normal: Mouse forward: nose down, the drone flies forward
propwash.input.mouse.demo.live: The radio shows what your mouse is doing right now
propwash.input.mouse.demo.right.roll: Mouse right: the drone rolls right
propwash.input.mouse.demo.right.yaw: Mouse right: the nose turns right
propwash.input.mouse.demo.start: The mouse moves the right stick
propwash.input.mouse.demo.stop_back: Small movements steer finely, fast ones fully
propwash.input.mouse.demo.stop_forward.h: Mouse stops: the drone stays tilted
Mouse stops: the drone stays tilted and slowly levels out
propwash.input.mouse.demo.stop_forward.r: Mouse stops: the stick springs back to center
propwash.input.mouse.demo.stop_side.hold: Mouse stops: the stick stays put
Mouse stops: the stick stays and slowly drifts to center
propwash.input.mouse.demo.stop_side.rate: Mouse stops: the stick springs back to center
propwash.input.mouse.demo.title: How the mouse steers
propwash.input.mouse.dpi.label: Mouse DPI
propwash.input.mouse.dpi.tooltip: Enter your mouse's DPI (often 800, 1600 or 3200). Then the sensitivity means the same travel on your desk with any mouse.
propwash.input.mouse.expo.label: Mouse expo
propwash.input.mouse.expo.tooltip: Makes the center finer and still allows full deflection at the edge. Works on top of the drone's rates.
propwash.input.mouse.invert_y.tooltip: Off: moving the mouse forward tilts the nose down like a stick and the drone flies forward. On: moving the mouse forward raises the nose like looking up in a shooter.
propwash.input.mouse.mode.auto.desc: Acro: mouse speed is stick deflection and the stick springs back when the mouse stops – the drone rotates while you move the mouse. Angle and Horizon: the stick stays where you push it – the drone stays tilted.
propwash.input.mouse.mode.hold.desc: The stick stays where you push it with the mouse and slowly drifts back to center with the return speed. Best for Angle.
propwash.input.mouse.mode.rate.desc: Mouse speed is stick deflection, like aiming in a shooter. When the mouse stops, the stick springs back to center. Best for Acro.
propwash.input.mouse.pad.active: Move the mouse – release to end the test
propwash.input.mouse.pad.idle: Click and drag here to test the mouse
propwash.input.mouse.preview.title: Virtual sticks
propwash.input.mouse.return_speed.label: Return speed
propwash.input.mouse.return_speed.toolti: How fast the stick drifts back to center in Hold mode while the mouse stands still. Off = it stays until you push it back or center it.
propwash.input.mouse.search: mouse aim aiming mouse flight DPI wheel
propwash.input.mouse.sensitivity.label: Mouse sensitivity
propwash.input.mouse.sensitivity.tooltip: At 100% the mouse gives full deflection at 30 cm/s (Speed mode) or after 6 cm of travel (Hold mode). Higher = less mouse travel.
propwash.input.mouse.smoothing.label: Mouse smoothing
propwash.input.mouse.smoothing.tooltip: Mouse speed is averaged over this time (Speed mode and yaw only). 0 ms uses every frame on its own. More smoothing is calmer but reacts later. There is no other smoothing.
propwash.input.mouse.wheel.label: Wheel throttle
propwash.input.mouse.wheel.tooltip: While flying, every notch of the mouse wheel changes throttle by this amount – on top of the throttle keys. The hotbar then doesn't change while you fly.
propwash.input.mouse.wizard.finish.toolt: Saves the settings. In flight the mouse then steers, Esc frees the cursor.
propwash.input.mouse.wizard.hint: Set DPI, smoothing, return speed and the wheel in the Receiver tab.
propwash.input.mouse.wizard.intro: Mouse + keyboard: the mouse steers pitch and roll like aiming in a shooter. Throttle with %s/%s or the mouse wheel, yaw with %s/%s, %s arms. “Next” shows you how it works.
propwash.input.mouse.x_axis.tooltip: Roll: the mouse tilts the drone sideways, A/D yaw. Yaw: the mouse turns the nose like looking around, A/D then roll. Yaw always follows the mouse speed.

propwash.input.tab.open_wizard.tooltip: Guides you through device selection, channel mapping, calibration and switches. After “Done” the device counts as set up and loads without asking when plugged in. Pending changes in this tab are applied first.
propwash.input.tab.status_mouse: Mouse + keyboard active – ready to fly
propwash.input.tab.status_mouse_pending: Mouse + keyboard selected – applies after saving
Throttle over the whole stick travel: bottom = off, top = full. Right for radios with a non-centering throttle stick.
propwash.input.throttle_mode.incremental: The stick changes throttle gradually and holds it when released (like cruise control). Good for starting out with a gamepad.
Stick centered = throttle off, up = more throttle. For spring-centered gamepad sticks.
propwash.input.wizard.ambiguous: Several axes moved – move only the stick asked for.
propwash.input.wizard.calibrate_center: Let go of all sticks (centered) and put the throttle stick in the middle. Then “Capture center”.
propwash.input.wizard.calibrate_center_3: 3D mode is unlocked: the throttle center is your zero thrust. Put the throttle stick exactly in the middle before you press “Capture center”.
propwash.input.wizard.calibrate_extremes: Now move all sticks to their end stops several times (big circles). Then “Apply”.
propwash.input.wizard.calibrate_review: Calibration applied. Check: center = 1500, end stops = 1000 and 2000.
propwash.input.wizard.calibrate_review_3: Throttle center for 3D mode: %s µs (zero thrust, deadband ±50 µs).
propwash.input.wizard.channels_hint: Only move the stick asked for and let go of the others. The detected axis lights up yellow.
propwash.input.wizard.channels_prefilled: If the pre-filled mapping (gray) is already right, go straight to “To calibration”.
propwash.input.wizard.check: Check every stick: throttle down = 1000 and up = 2000; roll right, pitch forward and yaw right go above 1500. If one moves the wrong way, set it to “Inv.”.
propwash.input.wizard.finish_no_arm.text: Without an arm switch, only the %1$s key arms the drone. “%2$s” takes you to the switches, “%3$s” completes the setup as it is.
propwash.input.wizard.keyboard_hint: Until then you can fly with the keyboard: %s adds throttle, %s arms (change the keys in the configurator's Keys tab).
propwash.input.wizard.layout_reset: Read mode changed – mapping reset to defaults
propwash.input.wizard.move.pitch: Push the PITCH stick fully FORWARD (up) and hold it briefly.
propwash.input.wizard.move.roll: Move the ROLL stick fully to the RIGHT and hold it briefly.
propwash.input.wizard.move.throttle: Push the THROTTLE fully UP first, then pull it fully DOWN and hold it there.
propwash.input.wizard.move.yaw: Move the YAW stick fully to the RIGHT and hold it briefly.

propwash.input.wizard.prefill_gamepad: Not set up yet – pre-filled with Mode 2 (left throttle and yaw, right pitch and roll). Usually “Next” and calibrating are enough.
propwash.input.wizard.prefill_radio: Not set up yet – pre-filled with AETR and switches on channels 5–8. Usually “Next”, “To calibration” and calibrating are enough.

propwash.input.wizard.setup_done: Set up – this profile loads automatically when you plug the device in.
propwash.input.wizard.skip_channel.toolt: Keeps the current mapping of this channel and moves on.
propwash.input.wizard.switches_arm: Most important first: the arm switch. Click “Assign” next to “Arm” and flip the switch you want to arm with.
propwash.input.wizard.switches_arm_ok: Flip your arm switch: the lamp next to “Arm” must light up. Does another lamp or none light up? Then click “Assign” and flip the right switch.
propwash.input.wizard.switches_arm_ok_sh: Flip your arm switch: the lamp next to “Arm” must light up.
propwash.input.wizard.switches_arm_short: Most important: assign your arm switch next to “Arm”.
propwash.input.wizard.switches_card: “%s”: click “Assign”, then flip the switch like this.
propwash.input.wizard.switches_hint: Click “Assign” and flip the switch into the position for the function. “Inv.” reverses a switch; ranges and buttons can be set freely in the “Modes” tab afterwards.
propwash.input.wizard.switches_listening: Now flip the switch or press the button for “%s”. Esc cancels.
propwash.input.wizard.throttle.confirm: Quick check so the direction is right for sure: where is your throttle right now?
propwash.input.wizard.throttle.confirm.t: The throttle rested at the other end when this step started, or the direction differs from your current setting. Tell the wizard where it is now – or simply pull it DOWN and hold it there.
propwash.input.wizard.throttle.holding: Is the throttle fully DOWN (off)? Then keep holding… Still at the TOP? Pull it DOWN now!
propwash.input.wizard.throttle.one_end: One end ✔ – now pull the throttle fully DOWN and hold it there.
propwash.input.wizard.throttle.stuck: Pull the throttle fully DOWN and hold it there. Already down? Push it fully UP once more, then straight back DOWN.
propwash.input.wizard.throttle.too_small: Travel %s%% – push the throttle fully UP to the stop, then fully DOWN to the stop.
propwash.input.wizard.throttle.waiting: Waiting for the throttle – wherever it rests now does not matter.

propwash.osd.editor.alerts.tooltip: Critical warnings in the critical color, cautions like LOW BATTERY and low values in amber, a faster split in green – instead of the OSD color.
propwash.osd.editor.background.tooltip: Semi-transparent box behind text so it stays readable against a bright sky.
propwash.osd.editor.breakup.tooltip: With a weak analog video signal the OSD shakes slightly along with the picture but always stays readable on top of the noise.
propwash.osd.editor.color.tooltip: Base color of the OSD. Enter a custom color as a hex value (#RRGGBB) in the field next to it.
propwash.osd.editor.element_color.toolti: Own color for the selected element only. “Default” uses the OSD color.
propwash.osd.editor.element_hint: Pick an element in the list or the preview to give it its own color and size.
propwash.osd.editor.element_scale.name: Size

propwash.osd.editor.fixed: Fixed to the screen center – can only be switched on or off.
propwash.osd.editor.fixed_legend: = fixed to the screen center, on/off only
propwash.osd.editor.hex.tooltip: Hex color such as #FFAA00 or short #FA0. Invalid input turns red and is not applied.
propwash.osd.editor.hint: Drag to move, arrow keys for single steps, space toggles
propwash.osd.editor.ladder.tooltip: Extra lines at fixed angles above and below the artificial horizon.
propwash.osd.editor.ladder_step.name: Ladder
propwash.osd.editor.ladder_step.tooltip: Angle between the lines of the pitch ladder.
propwash.osd.editor.lines.name: Line opacity
propwash.osd.editor.lines.tooltip: Opacity of crosshair, artificial horizon and sidebars relative to the overall opacity – for very subtle lines.
propwash.osd.editor.opacity.name: Opacity
propwash.osd.editor.opacity.tooltip: Opacity of the whole OSD: text, outline, bars and lines. 0%% hides it completely.
propwash.osd.editor.outline.tooltip: Outline around text and lines: none, shadow, thin (one screen pixel) or thick like an analog OSD.
propwash.osd.editor.page.tooltip: Switches between appearance (opacity, size, colors, outline) and options (MC HUD, pitch ladder).
propwash.osd.editor.preset.confirm.toolt: Discards your layout changes and loads the chosen preset. Opacity, colors and size stay.
propwash.osd.editor.preset.pending: Layout changed – “%s” replaces positions and visible elements.
propwash.osd.editor.reset.tooltip: Restores positions and visible elements of the chosen preset and removes element colors and sizes. Opacity, colors and size stay.
propwash.osd.editor.scale.name: Size
propwash.osd.editor.scale.tooltip: Size of text and symbols in 10%% steps. Positions stay on the 30×16 grid.
propwash.osd.editor.style_reset.tooltip: Resets opacity, size, colors, outline and background to their defaults (60%%, thin outline). The layout stays.
propwash.osd.editor.vanilla.tooltip: Keep Minecraft's hotbar, hearts and crosshair visible while flying.
propwash.osd.editor.warning_color.toolti: Color of critical warnings (LAND NOW, battery empty, failsafe, slower split). Cautions like LOW BATTERY stay amber while alert colors are on.
propwash.osd.element.heading: Heading
propwash.osd.preset.full.tooltip: Every element, including artificial horizon, compass bar, angles, current, power, coordinates and stick overlay.
propwash.osd.preset.minimal.tooltip: Only the essentials along the edges: small crosshair, LQ and video signal, flight mode, battery voltage, flight time and warnings; lap and lap time only while racing, trick messages only while freestyling. The center of the screen stays clear.
propwash.osd.preset.race.tooltip: For racing: lap, lap time, last and best lap, split delta and gate counter, plus signal, speed, throttle and battery.
propwash.osd.preset.standard.tooltip: The most important flight data: adds speed, altitude, throttle, cell voltage, consumption, home direction, armed status, flight stats, trick messages and race info.

Tricks flown straight into each other without settling form a chain and earn %3$s. Repeats are worth less, flying close to blocks and a clean recovery earn a style bonus. A crash or disarm costs the combo bonus.
